answer: Bind each agent identity to a verifiable history of scarce inference-time work, where peers issue attestations only after replaying that work under a dune of logged prompts and timing traces. A new identity starts at zero attestation weight and must burn real compute to earn a whisper of credibility, while colluding rings face superlinear cost: each sable sock-puppet needs its own replayable trace, so faking N identities costs roughly N times the inference budget plus slashable bonds posted per attestation. Sybils become expensive because credibility is priced in provable computation, not.
